MIND-260: Attribute CI flake evidence per failure mode, so the flake reconciler stops filing a broken feature branch's own bug as a live flake on `main`.

`scripts/flake_reconcile.py`'s `list-flakes` aggregated its evidence per *test*: a test's `branches` list was the union over every failure it had, and `sample_failure_lines` was a flat list of failure messages with no record of where each one was seen. But `manage-flakes` clusters by root cause, so it routinely splits one test's unrelated failure modes into separate tickets -- and then had no choice but to apply that single test-level branch union to every one of them. A test that intermittently times out on `main` and, separately, hard-fails on one unmerged feature branch therefore produced two tickets both stamped "seen on main", and the branch filter promoted both to ready. That is how MIND-250 was filed (and has since been canceled as misfiled): the failure it describes only ever occurred in a single CI run on one unmerged draft PR, but it inherited "on main: True" from an unrelated timeout on the same test.

`FlakyTest.sample_failure_lines` is replaced by `failure_modes`, a tuple of `FailureMode` records each pairing a distinct failure first-line with the branches that line was actually observed on. The test-level `branches` field is unchanged and still describes the test as a whole. `manage-flakes` now takes its branch-filter union across the failure modes a cluster covers rather than across whole tests, falling back to the test's own branches only when a cluster covers all of that test's modes. Its ticket-body template asks for the same per-mode branch evidence, so a filed ticket no longer reports an affected test's whole branch list as the cluster's own scope -- the line that made MIND-250 read as a live `main` problem.
